subject: Renewal: capacity, cost & term options for Aperture
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha@aperture.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@aperture.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — looking to right-size next term

Diego,

Hope you’re well. Our current term with Redwood expires mid-November and we’re starting procurement conversations. Two quick asks from our side: 1) a concise summary of our Q3 token spend and where the biggest cost drivers are, and 2) recommended commit/term options that would (a) reduce our per-token cost by at least ~18% and (b) give us headroom for a planned feature surge in Q1.

We’d like any options that keep latency SLAs for our chat endpoints (95th percentile < 180ms) — that’s non-negotiable. Can you share a short packet we can bring to procurement and a one-pager for execs?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Cole
Director of AI Products, Aperture Labs
--
Aperture Labs | aperture.com
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@aperture.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — looking to right-size next term

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled a concise package for procurement and an exec one-pager; attaching a CSV export of Q3 usage and a preliminary SOW template that contains the commit/term choices. High-level summary below and happy to jump on a 30m call this week to walk the team through numbers.

High-level observations:
- Q3 billable tokens: 1.8B (avg per-day growth ~12% MoM driven by chat & reranking).
- Top cost drivers: repeated long-context multi-turn sessions (prefix reuse low), and a small percentage (~6%) of high-temp sampling requests for exploratory features.
- Performance: 95th p90 latency for chat endpoints avg 160ms in us-west — within SLA but tight during peak.

Recommended options (short):
1) 12-month renewal, 20% commit uplift (+10% headroom burst credits), 10% list discount -> ~22% unit cost reduction after batching/caching recommendations applied.
2) 24-month renewal, 35% commit uplift, dedicated pool for chat (reduces p95 variance) -> ~30% unit cost reduction, priority capacity.
3) 9-month bridge with flexible burst credits (for Q1 surge) if procurement needs a shorter contract.

Attachments: Aperture_usage_Q3.csv, RDW_SOW_draft_v2.pdf

If you want, Marissa can add a short ROI slide showing token efficiency wins if we enable prefix/KV caching and set the default sampling policy.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — looking to right-size next term

Diego / team — attaching a token_breakdown_v1.xlsx (internal) and pasting a short health recap for the thread:

Operational health (Q3):
- Error rate: 0.6% (mostly transient 429s during one day of spike; mitigated by fallback to smaller model).
- Average tokens per session: 845 (std dev 220) — indicates many long multi-turn flows.
- Cache miss rate (prefix): 72% — opportunity to reduce token spend significantly by enabling automatic prefix/KV caching for identical flows.

Estimated savings (conservative, applied to current mix):
- Enable prefix caching + smart batching => ~14% token reduction.
- Move chat endpoints to dedicated pool with the 35% uplift option => additional ~9% latency-related efficiency (fewer retries, less sampling).
- Combined effect (with 24-month commit) => ~25% reduction in unit cost versus current list.

Risk notes:
- If you lock a 24-month commit, ensure we include an annual usage true-up clause and a quarterly review cadence.
- For a Q1 feature surge, recommend a 10–15% burst credit tranche on top of committed units rather than full overprovisioning — cheaper and more flexible.

Attachments referenced: token_breakdown_v1.xlsx

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@aperture.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal & pricing tiers (initial)

Samantha — following up with concrete pricing/term options (summary below). I’ve put the full SOW draft in the RDW_SOW_draft_v2.pdf attachment and annotated the commercial page for procurement.

Option A — 12 months- Commit: 2.2B tokens/yr (+20% vs current run-rate)- Discount: 10% off list + 12% operational credit (applied as monthly billing credit)- Burst credits: 10% pre-authorized- Expected unit outcome: ~22% cost reduction vs current list

Option B — 24 months (recommended for predictability)- Commit: 2.4B tokens/yr (+35% headroom)
- Discount: 18% off list + priority capacity SLA (4-hour mitigation target)
- Dedicated chat pool included (no separate infra charge for first 12 months)
- Expected unit outcome: ~30% cost reduction vs current list

Option C — 9-month bridge (procurement-friendly)- Commit: 1.9B tokens total
- Discount: 6% off list
- Flexible burst add-on for Q1 surge (pay-as-you-go pricing for burst)

Commercial asks from Redwood:
- Quarterly review meetings (Marissa to own).
- Usage true-up annually.
- Standard SOW with DocuSign link (attached).

Attachments: RDW_SOW_draft_v2.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through numbers with procurement today/tomorrow.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@aperture.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aperture.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & pricing tiers (initial)

Thanks for the options. Procurement and our platform team reviewed the SOW. A few items we need to see in the redline before we can submit to legal: 1) add a one-time SLA credit (pro-rated) for any monthly p95 violations beyond 2 incidents; 2) include a 12-months data retention export window in the Private deployment clause; 3) increase pre-authorized burst credits in Option B to 20% for the Q1 plan.

On pricing — Option B looks attractive but procurement prefers a 24-month with a 30% discount (we’re short of their target). If you can’t hit 30% we’d accept 18% + the extra 10% burst credits and a 6-month extension to the dedicated chat inclusion (i.e., dedicated pool free for 18 months).

Attached: Procurement_redline_comments.docx (sent separately to your procurement alias).

-Tom
Tom Barnes
VP, Platform Engineering, Aperture Labs
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@aperture.com>, procurement@aperture.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & pricing tiers (initial)

Tom / team — appreciate the clear redlines. We can accept the operational redlines with two notes: (A) SLA credit language — we’ll add the 1x pro-rated credit after the second p95 violation and a remediation plan clause; (B) Data export retention — 12 months is fine for Private clause but for hosted we’ll offer an optional archival export add-on (details in SOW).

Regarding pricing: we can do Option B with your requested commercial mix: 18% base discount + an additional one-time onboarding credit equal to ~5% of first-year committed spend (effectively brings economics close to your 24–30% target) and increase pre-authorized burst credits to 20% for Q1. We’ll also extend the dedicated pool complimentary period to 18 months.

Next steps:
- I’ll push an updated SOW with these redlines to DocuSign by EOD and attach a short one-pager for your procurement.
- Marissa will schedule the first quarterly review after contract execution.
- Procurement: if you can confirm DocuSign recipient list and signers, I’ll route the envelope.

Attachments in follow-up: RDW_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (with redlines), one-pager-exec-Aperture.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
